title: Flying with a baby: what to really expect
summary: Little ears, choosing seats, and what the crew can (and can't) do

sections.heading: Little ears
sections.text: Changes in air pressure during take-off and landing can make little ears uncomfortable. A feed, a bottle or a dummy can help, because sucking and swallowing helps balance the pressure. Landing is often the trickier part, so keep something back for the descent.

sections.heading: Choosing seats
list: On long-haul flights, bassinets fix to the bulkhead rows. Ask for one when you book
An aisle seat makes nappy-change trips easier
Babies can't sit in, or right next to, an emergency exit row

sections.heading: Your lap or their own seat?
sections.text: Babies under 2 can usually travel on your lap. The American Academy of Pediatrics says a baby is safest in their own seat in an approved car seat, so if that's an option for you, ask the airline which car seats they accept.

sections.heading: The crew
sections.text: They've seen it all before, and a crying baby is part of flying. Services differ between airlines, though. Ryanair, for example, says it doesn't warm baby bottles, so bring a flask or ready-made milk just in case.

tip.label: Gentle truth
tip.text: The flight is usually more manageable than the version in your head. And if your baby cries, the American Academy of Pediatrics says to feel free to ignore the stares. You're doing a good job.

title: How to pack: a first-timer's framework
summary: The rule of three and what you'll wish you'd left at home

sections.heading: The rule of three
sections.text: For any item that can get dirty (clothes, bibs, muslins), pack what you think you need — then add three more. Babies will always exceed your estimates at the worst moment.

sections.heading: What to leave behind
list: Baby bath — hotels have sinks, or buy a cheap inflatable locally
Baby monitor — keep baby in your room, problem solved
Every toy they own — two familiar toys maximum

sections.heading: What you can buy there
sections.text: Nappies, wipes and baby food are sold in most places. Formula is too, but brands and recipes differ, so if your baby is settled on one, bring enough from home. Save the luggage space for things that are harder to replace.

tip.label: Weight hack
tip.text: Wear your bulkiest items on the plane. Stuff muslins and socks into shoes in your bag.

title: Booking the right hotel for a baby
summary: Questions to ask before you confirm that non-refundable rate

sections.heading: Always confirm before booking
list: Do you have a cot/crib available, and what size mattress?
Is the room large enough for a travel cot on the floor?
Do you have blackout curtains — or can you provide a blind?
Is there a microwave or kettle in the room (for sterilising)?

sections.heading: Room location
sections.text: Request away from lifts, ice machines, and street-facing rooms. Ground floor for night-waking walks. Away from pool if you're a light sleeper — pumps run all night.

tip.label: Tip
tip.text: Suite-style rooms where the bedroom is separated from a living area are worth the upgrade — you can sit up after baby sleeps without a screen glow problem.
